thread:
mia: Hey team — Acme POC (acct: acme-demo-0987) is seeing 429s during a scheduled demo run around 03:10 UTC. They say it was fine yesterday. Asking if we have any short-term bridge for demos on the free plan.

sam: Can you drop their request/response sample + which endpoint (chat/generate/embeddings)? Need rate-limit headers too.

mia: Repro snippet from them:
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"large-batch"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 60
x-rw-quota-tier: free
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"concurrency limit reached"}
```

sam: Thanks. That looks like a concurrency ceiling + per-minute token cap. Free-tier defaults are fairly low — the combination of parallel workers + high token payloads will hit it quickly. Is this a short demo spike or a sustained ingest?

mia: Short demo, ~2 hours. Their harness fired ~15 concurrent workers at peak and they expected it to scale.

devops-bot: IncidentBot: quota-throttle detected for acme-demo-0987 at 2026-03-17T03:10:12Z. Suggested action: escalate to sales for temporary uplift.

anne-sales: I can do a 48h demo uplift (soft override) but need customer billing contact + expected peak QPS and token/min estimate. Once I have that I can provision a temporary increase and track billing. @sam any guardrails we should require?

sam: For short demos we usually allow a 3x concurrency uplift with autoscale caps. Recommend 48h, max concurrency 18, token cap ~600k/min and monitoring on latencies. Also enable exponential backoff on client side to avoid retry storms.

mia: Customer contact is jane@acme.com. They say expected peak ~18 QPS but most of the time <10. I'll ask them to reduce parallelism and enable backoff as a first step.

anne-sales: Cool — please open internal ticket SUP-4321 with the uplift request, expected window, and payment/contact info. I can flip the flag once PO/card is provided.

sam: Quick engineering mitigations: 1) add jittered exponential backoff, 2) reduce concurrent workers from 15-20 to 8-10, 3) enable caching for repeated prefixes to save tokens. If they can't change the client, the temporary uplift is safest.

mia: Filed SUP-4321 and attached the logs + curl output. I told them we'll follow up in ~30m after we get their payment contact. Thanks all :thumbsup:

anne-sales: I'll standby. If they agree to card/PO I can approve the 48h uplift within the hour.

sam: Also double-checked: sometimes customers have multiple API keys across services that sum against the same account-level quota. If they have CI or other jobs running, ask them to pause during the demo.

mia: Noted — pinging customer to pause other jobs. Will update thread with their response.

mia: (later) Customer confirmed they'll pause nightly ingest and provided PO contact. Anne, forwarding PO now.

anne-sales: Received PO, provisioning the override. I'll post the duration and caps once done. :white_check_mark:
